messages.author: c8f3cf85832ac2f7
messages.subject: ReferenceClass documentation
parts:
A few weeks back, I put together some thoughts about how best to document ReferenceClass (RC) generator objects and their methods. 

Basically, the real point of contention is how to document RC methods. The official guidance is that they should not be documented in separate Rd files, but rather that (brief?) docstrings could be used. But what if the method requires more extensive documentation? I would love to get some engagement with the ideas that I've put together in the gist, especially now that Hadley's begun to support RC method docs through the github hosted version of roxygen.

Cheers

messages.author: c8f3cf85832ac2f7
messages.subject: Re: ReferenceClass documentation
parts:
On Wednesday, 8 January 2014 08:14:50 UTC+11, Hadley Wickham wrote:
Hi Imanuel,

Two questions:

* How do you imagine the longer docstrings being included in the Rd files?

Only the leading line of the docstring would be included in the RC generator object Rd file (per `promptClass()` output). It seems like the official guidance is that the docstring output is the place to find help on RC methods (as they explicitly state that they should not be documented in Rd files - presumably standalone to the RC generator object Rd file).

* Why create a new format for docstrings? Why not make them use the
regular roxygen formatting?

The way I see it, roxygen markup is useful for almost everywhere because it allows Rd files to be generated. It is lightweight. But of course, there's a lot that doesn't need to be there if you aren't creating Rd files. Assuming that I am right and that RC methods should not be documented in stand alone Rd files, then you could replace the roxygen markup with something more lightweight like markdown (e.g. instead of @param foo, you could use `foo`, with some indentation). However, if roxygen is processing the first line of the docstring, it might run into some difficulty if you are adoring the first line with markdown syntax that roxygen doesn't like. 

So, in summary, RC method documentation would be split between:

1. Docstring that contains fuller documentation
2. Brief explanation of method in the RC generator object Rd file. This could perhaps be the first line of docstring.

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: ReferenceClass documentation
parts:
>> * How do you imagine the longer docstrings being included in the Rd files?
>>
>
> Only the leading line of the docstring would be included in the RC generator
> object Rd file (per `promptClass()` output). It seems like the official
> guidance is that the docstring output is the place to find help on RC
> methods (as they explicitly state that they should not be documented in Rd
> files - presumably standalone to the RC generator object Rd file).

What would happen to the other lines?

Regardless of what reference class documentation states, I think the
vast majority of RC docs need to end up in Rd files. It's ok if
they're accessible via $help() as well, but most people won't know to
look there.

>> * Why create a new format for docstrings? Why not make them use the
>> regular roxygen formatting?
>
> The way I see it, roxygen markup is useful for almost everywhere because it
> allows Rd files to be generated. It is lightweight. But of course, there's a
> lot that doesn't need to be there if you aren't creating Rd files. Assuming
> that I am right and that RC methods should not be documented in stand alone
> Rd files, then you could replace the roxygen markup with something more
> lightweight like markdown (e.g. instead of @param foo, you could use `foo`,
> with some indentation). However, if roxygen is processing the first line of
> the docstring, it might run into some difficulty if you are adoring the
> first line with markdown syntax that roxygen doesn't like.
>
> So, in summary, RC method documentation would be split between:
>
> 1. Docstring that contains fuller documentation
> 2. Brief explanation of method in the RC generator object Rd file. This
> could perhaps be the first line of docstring.

I pretty strongly believe if you're going to write more documentation
in the docstring, it should end up in an Rd file _somewhere_, and I
suspect if it's long, it should go in its own Rd file. But that would
involve creating some conventions for what a standalone Rd file should
look like - in particularly generating a usage statement that was both
useful and passed R CMD check might be challenging.

Hadley

On Thursday, 9 January 2014 10:06:04 UTC+11, Hadley Wickham wrote:
>> * How do you imagine the longer docstrings being included in the Rd files?
>>
>
> Only the leading line of the docstring would be included in the RC generator
> object Rd file (per `promptClass()` output). It seems like the official
> guidance is that the docstring output is the place to find help on RC
> methods (as they explicitly state that they should not be documented in Rd
> files - presumably standalone to the RC generator object Rd file).

What would happen to the other lines?

Regardless of what reference class documentation states, I think the
vast majority of RC docs need to end up in Rd files. It's ok if
they're accessible via $help() as well, but most people won't know to
look there.

The other lines would stay in the docstring and can be extracted using `$help()`. 

I am worried about ignoring the official RC guidance at two levels:

1. users will end up confused. 
2. the core team will get upset

One mitigating strategy to the second concern (not much you can do about the first) is to refer users to Rd based documentation in the docstring - something along the lines of "See `?RCMethod` for more complete documentation".  I could live with that. But it's still an additional step for the user. As to whether they will know to use `$help()`: that's a good point. However, given the guidance in the ReferenceClass documentation, I would hope that users will figure it out. Package level documentation would clearly indicate that the object is an RC and has certain methods (and possibly even indicate how these might be accessed).

I think duplicating the same docs in docstring and Rd is unnecessary and could lead to conflicting document in certain circumstances.

>> * Why create a new format for docstrings? Why not make them use the
>> regular roxygen formatting?
>
> The way I see it, roxygen markup is useful for almost everywhere because it
> allows Rd files to be generated. It is lightweight. But of course, there's a
> lot that doesn't need to be there if you aren't creating Rd files. Assuming
> that I am right and that RC methods should not be documented in stand alone
> Rd files, then you could replace the roxygen markup with something more
> lightweight like markdown (e.g. instead of @param foo, you could use `foo`,
> with some indentation). However, if roxygen is processing the first line of
> the docstring, it might run into some difficulty if you are adoring the
> first line with markdown syntax that roxygen doesn't like.
>
> So, in summary, RC method documentation would be split between:
>
> 1. Docstring that contains fuller documentation
> 2. Brief explanation of method in the RC generator object Rd file. This
> could perhaps be the first line of docstring.

I pretty strongly believe if you're going to write more documentation
in the docstring, it should end up in an Rd file _somewhere_, and I
suspect if it's long, it should go in its own Rd file.  But that would
involve creating some conventions for what a standalone Rd file should
look like - in particularly generating a usage statement that was both
useful and passed R CMD check might be challenging.

There is something quite zen about docstrings - particularly as it gets rid of the need to process roxygen mark up to get Rd files.
 
Hadley

>> look there.
>
> The other lines would stay in the docstring and can be extracted using
> `$help()`.

Hmm, so at least you'd need a note in the doc saying to look at
$help() for more. That seems backwards to me - I'd think you'd want
the full docs accessible in the regular help, and a basic summary
available interactively.

> I am worried about ignoring the official RC guidance at two levels:
>
> 1. users will end up confused.
> 2. the core team will get upset

My response to this is:

1. Users are already confused. I don't think people even know how to
use S4 documentation and that's been around for years. Also, you
shouldn't need to know the details of what OO system you're using in
order to get help!

2. There's no point in worrying about that. You can spend a lot of
time avoiding something that you think will upset them, only to upset
them with something else. With roxygen2, I'll also happy to take all
the heat on any design decisions.

> One mitigating strategy to the second concern (not much you can do about the
> first) is to refer users to Rd based documentation in the docstring -
> something along the lines of "See `?RCMethod` for more complete
> documentation". I could live with that. But it's still an additional step
> for the user. As to whether they will know to use `$help()`: that's a good
> point. However, given the guidance in the ReferenceClass documentation, I
> would hope that users will figure it out. Package level documentation would
> clearly indicate that the object is an RC and has certain methods (and
> possibly even indicate how these might be accessed).
>
> I think duplicating the same docs in docstring and Rd is unnecessary and
> could lead to conflicting document in certain circumstances.

But it would never conflict because the Rd is already generated from
the docstring.

>> I pretty strongly believe if you're going to write more documentation
>> in the docstring, it should end up in an Rd file _somewhere_, and I
>> suspect if it's long, it should go in its own Rd file. But that would
>> involve creating some conventions for what a standalone Rd file should
>> look like - in particularly generating a usage statement that was both
>> useful and passed R CMD check might be challenging.
>
> There is something quite zen about docstrings - particularly as it gets rid
> of the need to process roxygen mark up to get Rd files.

I think that's a stronger argument if you were starting a
documentation system from scratch. While docstrings are definitely a
better approach than Rd files (and maybe better than roxygen comment
blocks), we have to work within the existing ecosystem of tools that
people know how to use.

Hadley

If there was a good convention for mapping from the class + method
